title: Substitute silicon access transistors with nanoelectromechanical contact relays
idea: Each cell's access device is a sub-100 nm NEM relay (TiN cantilever over a vapor-HF-released air gap) that physically disconnects its capacitor; off-leakage is zero, so a 0.3 fF planar BEOL capacitor and a ~0.4 V pull-in design suffice, built with a 180-90 nm MEMS toolset above logic.
why: Constraint: zero leakage, tiny C and 0.4 V give >=10x lower cell and bitline energy and remove refresh; facet: no EUV, mature-node MEMS fabs. Contact wear versus unlimited endurance is the big risk.

title: Eliminate deposited channels in 3D tiers: ion-cut transfer of single-crystal films
idea: For each 3D tier, bond and Smart-Cut a 20-50 nm single-crystal Si film from a donor wafer onto the finished tier below, build the lateral transistors at <=500 C with laser anneal, and reuse the donor dozens of times.
why: Fact 2: gives 3D DRAM a crystalline lateral transistor without Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy and its 26+ tier stack etch, cutting epi tool count and stack-etch risk.

title: HCl-vapor lateral SiGe recess builds fluorine-free stacked 3D DRAM tiers
idea: Extreme user: AI KV-cache racks that need capacity density above all. In Si/SiGe superlattice 3D DRAM, cut the lateral cavities for capacitors and transistors with HCl vapor at ~600C, which etches SiGe selectively, instead of CF4/O2 or HF/H2O2 etches.
why: 3D DRAM: makes the ~26+ tier lateral-recess module fluorine-free and epi-compatible, removing a key process blocker.

title: Razor-blade coatings: tetrahedral amorphous carbon deep-etch hardmasks
idea: Razor blades and engine parts are coated with ta-C (>70% sp3 diamond-like carbon) by filtered cathodic arc; use 100-200 nm boron-optional ta-C as the hardmask for capacitor and contact deep etch in place of thick amorphous-carbon and tungsten-doped carbon hardmasks.
why: Etch capital (facts 1, 4): ~2-3x the selectivity of a-C, so a thinner mask, lower total AR and ~20-30% shorter etch; C and B only, no W.

title: Helium-free fab: closed-loop chuck gas recapture and substitutes
idea: Po: the fab breathes no helium. Retrofit existing etch/CVD electrostatic chucks with closed-loop backside-gas recirculation and membrane purification, substitute H2/Ar or N2 where heat-transfer margin allows, and recover He from leak-check and stage purges.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline): cuts fab helium purchases ~80-90%, protecting output of existing lines.

title: Synaptic-vesicle quantal storage: count charged ferritin dots per cell
idea: Synapses signal in discrete vesicle quanta; dip-coat 15 ferritin-derived 7 nm oxide cores as separate islands over a 1.5 nm tunnel oxide on each oxide-semiconductor channel, charge 0-15 islands by direct tunnelling (ns writes, high endurance, ~100 ms retention, refreshed like DRAM) and read the step-quantized channel current as 4 bits.
why: 4 bits per cell in a capacitorless cell about 2.5x smaller than 6F2 gives ~10x bits/mm2; the dots self-assemble in a dip step, so wafer cost is nearly unchanged (facts 1, 4).

title: Lattice stepper: a single-pattern projection tool built domestically
idea: Because array layers are one repeating motif, build a stripped-down U.S. DUV projection tool with a permanently mounted mask, no reticle exchange and relaxed stitching, exposing only that motif while periphery runs elsewhere.
why: Tool cost ~$10-20M vs $70-200M, and simple enough for a domestic optics base (fused silica, lens grinding, U.S. excimer lasers).

title: Solar porous-silicon lift-off: reusable seed wafers for DRAM substrates
idea: Adapt the PV kerfless process: anodize a porous-silicon double layer on a reusable 300 mm CZ seed, grow a 10-20 um device-grade epitaxial Si film, bond it to a cheap handle (reclaimed or multicrystalline Si), and cleave along the porous layer; the seed is re-polished and reused 20-50 times.
why: Scarce resources (high-purity quartz crucibles, polysilicon, CZ pullers): prime CZ silicon per wafer drops ~20x. Risk: epi defect density versus the retention tail.

title: Ionogel double-layer capacitors replace 70:1 dielectric pillars
idea: Inverts 'the storage dielectric is a solid insulator'. Fill shallow cups with a confined solid-polymer ionogel so charge sits in a nanometre electric double layer (~20-40 uF/cm2 vs ~7 for ZrO2), meeting 5 fF at AR ~15:1, with blocking electrodes to suppress Faradaic leakage.
why: Removes the hardest high-AR etch and ALD fill (fact 1) with 3-5x charge per area; must prove ns-scale ion response in sub-10 nm confinement.

title: Crucible-free kerfless DRAM substrates via porous-silicon epitaxial lift-off
idea: Box: any cell x any access x any sense x 2D monolithic x epitaxial Si foil on a reusable seed x CVD epitaxy. One CZ seed wafer is anodized into double-layer porous Si and sealed by H2 anneal; a 50-100 um device-grade epi layer is grown, bonded to a recycled-Si or glass carrier and lifted off, and the seed is reused 20-50 times.
why: Scarce resources: cuts Spruce Pine high-purity-quartz crucible use and CZ pulling per wafer by ~20-50x and eliminates slicing kerf; substrate is ~5-10% of DRAM wafer cost.

title: Drawn coaxial-fibre bundles sliced into capacitor wafers
idea: Revive 1960s microchannel-plate and fibre-optic faceplate manufacturing: draw a preform of metal-core / high-k glass / metal-shell coaxial fibres in a nitrogen-purged tower, bundle and redraw three times to ~60 nm pitch, then slice the boule into 5 um wafers, each holding billions of parallel coaxial capacitors at AR ~80-100. Bond the slice to the transistor wafer so each landing pad catches several capacitors, averaging out random placement.
why: Facts 1 and 4: aspect ratio is set by slice thickness, not by etch, so AR 100+ needs no plasma, no litho and no rare gas, from ~$5-10M draw towers. Risks are metal/glass co-drawing below 100 nm and bond yield.

title: Anodized-alumina pores as a ready-made capacitor forest
idea: Inverts 'storage nodes must be individually patterned'. Anodize sputtered aluminium in oxalic acid so it self-orders into hexagonal pores (~25-60 nm pitch, AR >100:1); a 180 nm stepper only fences cell groups, and atomic-layer-epitaxy reactors of the 1990s TFEL-display type line the pores with electrode/dielectric/electrode, several pores in parallel per cell.
why: Self-assembled high-AR template from an electrochemistry bath; ~30x capacitor area per footprint so a 180 nm-rule cell gets ample Cs in a thin layer (fact 1).

title: Substitute photoresist patterning with block-copolymer self-assembly for capacitor honeycomb
idea: Cylinder-forming PS-b-PMMA (or high-chi PS-b-PDMS) packs naturally into the same hexagonal lattice as DRAM storage nodes; a sparse ArF guide pattern (one post per 3-4 sites) registers the film and the polymer fills in the rest, then PMMA cores are removed and transferred into the hard mask. One DUV exposure plus spin-coat and 250 C bake replaces a double-EUV or SAQP hole sequence.
why: Fact 4: 3-4x density multiplication from one cheap exposure; removes 1-2 EUV layers and the hex-array LELE overlay budget.

title: Bubble-memory chevron ratchets driven by one global rotating field
idea: Revive 1970s bubble memory's key trick, a global rotating in-plane field that moves every domain one step per cycle along permalloy chevrons: nanoimprint asymmetric pinning chevrons into e-beam-evaporated Co/Pt or ferrimagnetic multilayers (no argon sputtering) and drive all tracks with a GHz rotating field from two crossed package striplines. No per-track transistor or current is needed; only read and write heads sit at the loop ends.
why: Fact 4 and capital: one imprint plus two coarse metal masks define the array, with no EUV and no rare gas; a major/minor-loop layout with 64-bit minor loops stepping ~1 ns gives ~50 ns access. Risks are GHz field strength and domain stability below 50 nm.

title: Mars-perchlorate Cl2/O2 cyclic deep etch revives silicon trench capacitors
idea: Extreme user: a Mars fab where perchlorate soil yields chlorine but not fluorine. Etch deep trench capacitors into crystalline silicon with alternating HBr/Cl2 etch and O2 sidewall-oxidation passivation cycles (a chlorine Bosch process), then line them with ALD ZrO2/TiN.
why: Capacitor wall: the trench uses silicon depth under the cell (AR 80:1 possible) instead of a tall oxide mold, freeing surface for 3D stacking with no fluorocarbon gas.

title: (110)-silicon TMAH crystallographic etch makes 100:1 plasma-free trench capacitors
idea: Extreme user: MEMS inertial sensors for missiles, which etch vertical {111} walls in (110) silicon wet. Lay the cell array along <111> directions on (110) wafers and etch atomically smooth trenches in TMAH through an ALD Al2O3 mask, with no plasma and no fluorine.
why: Capacitor wall/capital: batch wet etch replaces single-wafer HAR plasma etchers (~$10M each) and gives AR >100:1 with smooth walls for reliable ALD.

title: Eliminate die-by-die thermocompression bonders: wafer-on-wafer HBM core stacking
idea: Hybrid-bond whole core-die wafers on top of each other and dice finished stacks, replacing hundreds of slow pick-and-place TCB bonds per wafer with one bond per layer; the base die still speaks standard HBM3E/HBM4.
why: Fact 6 and capital: removes the TCB bonder bottleneck that limits HBM output, with ~10x stacking throughput per tool; best paired with spare-die repair to offset compounded yield.

title: Capacitor-first DRAM: anneal the dielectric before transistors exist
idea: Inverts 'transistor first, capacitor last'. Etch and fill the storage-capacitor array into a bare carrier wafer, anneal the dielectric at 800-1000 C to crystallize ultra-high-k phases (rutile TiO2, SrTiO3, k 80-150) that a finished transistor could never survive, then Smart-Cut-transfer a thin single-crystal Si film on top and build access transistors aligned to the buried capacitor marks.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): k~100 lets pillar AR fall from ~70:1 to ~35:1, removing the slowest high-AR etch/fill steps and their tool count; ~10-15% fewer process hours per wafer.

title: Fluidic self-assembly of tiny DRAM confetti dies raises yield
idea: Extreme user: smart dust and RFID tags assembled in fluid. Dice DRAM into 0.2 mm^2 'confetti' chiplets by plasma dicing, then let them settle by shape into recesses on an interposer in a liquid bath, assembling thousands per minute without pick-and-place.
why: Yield/capital: tiny dies have near-100% yield at immature processes, so new fabs sell output in months; assembly cost per die falls ~10x.

title: Capillary condensation fills only narrow array gaps, eliminating block masks
idea: Effect: capillary condensation (Kelvin equation). Below saturation, a precursor vapor such as a silazane condenses only in gaps narrower than the Kelvin radius (~10-20 nm), so dense array trenches fill while wide periphery stays open; a cure turns the liquid into oxide. $1M tests the effect on test arrays at university fabs within 24 months.
why: Fact 4: each array/periphery block mask removed saves a litho plus etch pass; Kelvin-selective fill could drop 1-3 block masks per flow.

title: Sourdough crumb: porous-silicon capacitors cut by one isolation mask
idea: Like dough fermenting gas pockets, electrochemically porosify a 1 um doped poly-Si layer over the landing pads into ~20 nm random pores, coat with high-k and TiN by ALD, and use the single added coarse mask to cut a cell-isolation grid, so each cell's capacitor is whatever ~15-25 pores fall in it.
why: Fact 1: 10-30x surface-area gain with no hole litho or HAR etch; Cs spread handled by pad sizing and sense-margin binning; bath tool ~1/20 the cost of HAR etch.

title: Urban-mining line requalifies retired server DRAM
idea: Inverts 'new supply needs new wafers'. Robotic hot-air reflow strips DRAM packages from retired server DIMMs, a 48-hour retention and row-hammer stress screen sorts them, and they are re-mounted on CXL memory-expander cards for pooled tiers.
why: Hundreds of millions of GB retire yearly; recovered supply at ~10-20% of new-wafer capital per GB, zero EUV.

title: Substitute 3 V boosted wordlines with negative-capacitance steep-slope access transistors
idea: Add a thin HZO layer to the access-transistor gate stack, capacitance-matched for negative-capacitance amplification (sub-60 mV/dec), so the same off-leakage is reached with a ~1 V wordline; the VPP charge pumps and the thick-gate-oxide periphery module with its masks are deleted.
why: Constraint and fact 10: wordline CV2 falls ~9x and ~30%-efficient pump losses vanish, giving >=10x on the row path; facet: removes 3-5 masks for dual/triple oxides.

title: Block-copolymer hexagonal holes with alumina infiltration replace EUV capacitor layer
idea: Extreme user: an EUV-less fab. Self-assemble non-fluorinated PS-b-PMMA into a hexagonal hole lattice at ~24 nm pitch on a guide pattern, harden the PMMA with sequential-infiltration Al2O3 (TMA/H2O) or remove it with UV + acetic acid, and transfer with Cl2/HBr.
why: Litho: replaces 1-2 EUV exposures for the capacitor array with a coat-and-bake step; the infiltration hardmask survives chlorine transfer.

title: Lensless displacement-Talbot printing of cell arrays with metal-oxo resist
idea: Extreme user: an EUV-less regional fab. Self-image a single cheap grating mask onto the wafer by displacement-Talbot proximity printing at 193 nm, which halves the pitch with no projection lens, into a fluorine-free tin/hafnium-oxo resist.
why: Litho capital: a ~$5M tool prints periodic DRAM array layers in place of ~$200M EUV exposures; no PFAS photoacid generators.

title: Memory futures: decade offtake contracts pre-fund new DRAM fabs
idea: Shift capital timing: hyperscalers buy 10-year capacity futures with upfront pre-delivery payments (as airlines do for aircraft), which collateralize fab construction loans and set a price band.
why: Moves capital intensity off the memory maker's balance sheet; ~30% of fab capex pre-funded lowers the cost of capital by several points.

title: Croissant lamination: binary-tree bonding of tested half-stacks for 3D DRAM
idea: Random stimulus 'croissant' (fold dough, layers double) -> 3D DRAM tiers are built as single-crystal SOI-like silicon layers by smart-cut transfer, merged pairwise in parallel (1+1 -> 2, 2+2 -> 4, ... -> 32). Every sub-stack is e-beam- and probe-tested before merging, so bad half-stacks are discarded early instead of poisoning a finished 32-tier wafer.
why: No manufacturable 3D cell (fact 2): bonded layers give perfect lateral-transistor silicon without Si/SiGe superlattice epitaxy. Tree merging cuts serial cycle time from N to log2(N) bond steps and turns multiplicative tier-yield loss into screened yield.

title: Optical-disc stamper family tree for DRAM array nanoimprint
idea: Adapt CD/DVD/Blu-ray replication: one e-beam-written quartz master is electroformed into nickel 'father', 'mother' and 'son' stampers (each generation multiplies copies ~10x), and the sons serve as UV-nanoimprint working templates for the periodic array layers (capacitor holes, landing pads, bitlines). Each son is retired after a fixed imprint count, as disc plants do, so defects never accumulate; EUV is kept only for the periphery.
why: Litho capital (fact 4): replaces 3-4 of the 5-7 EUV array exposures with NIL tools at ~1/5 the cost and ~1/10 the power of an EUV scanner; claim 15-25% wafer-cost cut. Risks: overlay at 12 nm-class pitch and imprint defectivity.

title: Open reticle: a shared public DRAM array mask set
idea: Reverse mask ownership: a government-backed consortium funds and qualifies one open DRAM array mask set and process recipe, licensed cheaply to new fabs, which only pay for their own periphery masks.
why: Mask sets cost $20-50M+ and take years to qualify; sharing them lowers the entry barrier for U.S. newcomers by that amount and saves 1-2 years.

title: Liquid-metal membrane chuck replaces helium backside cooling
idea: Combine the electrostatic chuck with a sealed, compliant membrane filled with gallium-indium liquid metal or a phase-change medium that conducts heat from the wafer backside. This removes the helium backside gas used in every etch and deposition chamber.
why: Helium is a chokepoint, with Qatar's ~30% offline since March 2026, and a DRAM fab runs thousands of He-cooled chambers. Removing He dependence also improves temperature uniformity for capacitor etch.

title: Hydrogen-cooled power generators: helium-free wafer chuck cooling
idea: Large power-plant generators are cooled with hydrogen because its thermal conductivity beats helium's; replace helium backside gas in etch, deposition and implant electrostatic chucks with low-pressure H2 or forming gas from on-site electrolysis, using the generator industry's purity monitoring and leak detection.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline; He is not Earth-abundant in practice): H2 ~0.18 W/m-K versus He ~0.15 keeps high-AR etch running through a helium crisis.

title: Helium-free chucks using liquid-metal backside contact
idea: Minify helium use to zero: replace helium backside cooling in etch and deposition chucks with a thin gallium-alloy film or compliant metal pads that conduct heat to the wafer.
why: Scarce resource: helium supply (Qatar ~30%, offline) currently gates fab output; removes a chokepoint for every wafer step.

title: Elephant-ear vein chucks end helium backside cooling in fab tools
idea: Elephants shed heat through dense vein networks in thin ears; build electrostatic chucks with an embedded two-phase microchannel 'vein' network under a 0.5 mm ceramic face and a compliant nanostructured graphite contact layer, replacing helium backside gas in etch and deposition chambers.
why: Removes helium dependence (Qatar ~30% of supply offline) across dozens of etch/ALD tools per fab, a scarce-resource risk that can idle lines.

title: Helium-free plasma tools: hydrogen backside gas, textured chucks
idea: Inverts 'etch and deposition chucks need helium backside cooling'. Use low-pressure H2 or H2/Ne backside gas (thermal conductivity ~1.2x He) with a micro-textured AlN chuck face and closed-loop recapture of all purge gas.
why: Helium is a live chokepoint (Qatar offline since March 2026); substitution plus recapture could cut fab helium use >90% at low capex.

title: Vending machine: tool vendors own tools, fab pays per wafer pass
idea: Random stimulus 'vending machine' (owner stocks it, you pay per item) -> lithography, etch and deposition OEMs own and maintain tools inside a new DRAM fab and bill per wafer pass, with uptime guarantees, backed by a federal loan guarantee pool.
why: Capital intensity (depreciation ~55% of wafer cost, fact 4) turns into variable cost. A U.S. entrant's upfront capex could fall ~50-60%, and OEMs gain recurring revenue.

title: Hydrogen-backside electrostatic chucks free etch and deposition from helium
idea: Box: unchanged cell x fab-method axis set to backside thermal gas. Replace helium backside cooling on electrostatic chucks (capacitor cryo-etch, CVD, ALD) with low-pressure H2 or forming gas, whose thermal conductivity (~0.18 W/m-K) matches helium, inside a closed recirculating plenum with on-site electrolytic H2, catalytic recombiner and leak sensors.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline): backside cooling and leak check are the main fab helium uses; removing them de-risks wafer output; risk is safety qualification and edge-plasma interaction.

title: Hydrogen backside gas frees etch chucks from Qatari helium
idea: Worse: keep helium backside cooling on every etch and deposition chuck while Qatar's supply is offline. Flip: switch electrostatic chucks to hydrogen backside gas (thermal conductivity ~1.2x helium, already plumbed in fabs) or a compliant CNT thermal pad for clean chambers, and requalify cryo high-AR etch uniformity.
why: Scarce resource: removes a ~30%-Qatar-dependent input from every plasma tool and prevents shortage-driven tool downtime.

title: Ti: getter-pumped vacuum wafer highway so wafers never see air
idea: Link etch, deposition and anneal tools with a titanium-getter/NEG-pumped vacuum transport spine and sealed vacuum carriers, so native oxide and airborne contamination never form and most cleans disappear; cleanroom air shrinks to tool-scale vacuum.
why: Water: attacks the two biggest users at once, cleans and cleanroom HVAC (humidification and chilled water), toward a 10x fab-level cut; also shrinks cleanroom capex.

title: Grow capacitor pillars upward instead of etching 70:1 holes
idea: Inverts 'deep features are carved top-down'. Pattern only a thin hard mask of seed openings, then grow single-crystal Si or TiN-clad nanopillars upward by selective-area epitaxy/CVD to 2-3 um (AR >100:1) and wrap them with ALD dielectric and plate; height becomes a growth-time knob instead of a plasma-selectivity limit.
why: Removes the deepest, slowest plasma etch and its bowing/twisting yield loss (facts 1, 4); AR ~115 reached with no extra litho, ~25% more charge per cell.

title: Eliminate signal TSVs between HBM core dies: inductive-coupling vertical links
idea: Replace the thousands of signal TSVs in core dies with on-chip coil pairs that couple data and clock between neighboring thinned dies, keeping only a few large power vias; the base die still presents a standard HBM3E/HBM4 PHY to the GPU.
why: Fact 6: removes most deep-via etch, liner, Cu fill, reveal and micro-bumps, recovering part of the ~3x area-per-bit tax and the 20-30% stack yield loss.

title: Bond cheap-logic periphery under a minimal-mask array wafer
idea: Split the die across two wafers: the 49% periphery is built on a mature 28 nm logic wafer, the array on a stripped-down ~15-mask array-only wafer, and the two are joined by wafer-to-wafer hybrid bonding at sub-1 um pitch.
why: Periphery stops consuming the expensive DRAM process (Fact 7): array density +40-60% and each wafer runs on the tool set where it is cheapest.

title: Substitute logic ALUs with bit-serial adders drawn from DRAM array masks
idea: Reserve every 64th mat edge for a strip of 1-bit full adders and latches built only from the array's own access transistors and capacitors as dynamic logic, on the same pitch, so no periphery masks are added; tensors are reduced bit-serially along the sense-amp row and operands never leave the mat.
why: Constraint: skips I/O and global-bus energy (most of DDR5's 10-20 pJ/bit) for >10x lower energy per elementwise or reduction operation; capital: zero new process steps.

title: Score-and-snap glass cutting: notch mask guides crack-defined trenches
idea: Use the single added coarse mask only to place notch crack-starters in a tensile SiN film; a thermal shock then propagates straight, few-nm-wide cracks between notches like scoring and snapping glass, and the cracks are transferred as ultra-narrow cut trenches isolating wordlines or active areas.
why: Fact 4: sub-5 nm cuts over long runs from a DUV mask, replacing an EUV cut layer.

title: Open capacitorless memory macro qualified at every U.S. logic fab
idea: Ideal: every fab already in the country is a memory fab. Closest: a CHIPS-funded open PDK macro (gain-cell array, sense amps, refresh controller) qualified on Intel 18A, TSMC Arizona, GlobalFoundries and SkyWater flows, so any U.S. chip can carry hundreds of MB on-die and GB-class stacked working memory without a DRAM fab.
why: U.S. manufacturability and capital: zero new fab capex; turns logic wafer starts into memory supply and cuts off-chip DRAM demand for caches and KV buffers.

title: Selective-area ALD grows storage contact and bottom electrode as one
idea: Ideal: contact and capacitor are one object made in one step. Closest: inhibitor SAMs on oxide let TiN or Ru ALD/CVD nucleate only on doped-Si landing pads and grow bottom-up through the mold, forming the storage-node plug and the capacitor bottom electrode continuously with no CMP or recess.
why: Facts 4 and 7: deletes one litho layer, one CMP, one etch-back plus metrology; removes an interface that adds contact resistance; ~3-5% fewer steps.

title: Child's LEGO stamp: nanoimprint the three most periodic array layers
idea: A child asks why you photograph the same honeycomb billions of times instead of stamping it. Replace EUV on the most periodic array layers (active-area lines, buried wordline, storage-node landing-pad holes) with jet-and-flash UV nanoimprint fed by a master-daughter template tree (one e-beam master spawns ~1,000 replicas, each good for ~10k wafers); DUV keeps the periphery.
why: Removes ~3 of 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4); an imprint tool is ~1/5 the price and ~1/10 the power of an EUV scanner; claim ~8-12% lower wafer cost and less single-supplier exposure. Risks: defectivity and overlay at 12 nm.

title: Fuse defective DRAM dies into half-capacity IoT memory grades
idea: Extreme user: $1 IoT boards that need 64-512 Mb, not 16 Gb. At wafer sort, map failing banks and laser-fuse dies with dead banks into 1/2 or 1/4-capacity SKUs with a standard remapped address space instead of scrapping them (HBM core dies included).
why: Raises sellable bits per wafer ~5-15% at zero added fab capital; pulls low-end demand off leading-edge good-die supply.

title: Crystal-plane etch: the silicon lattice draws the trenches
idea: Reverse plasma-defined walls to crystal-defined walls: on (110) silicon wafers, a coarse KrF mask opens slots and anisotropic wet etch (TMAH-like) stops on vertical {111} planes, giving atomically smooth, ultra-high-AR buried-wordline or capacitor trenches.
why: Wet benches instead of high-end etchers and no EUV; AR of 100:1+ is possible, so trench cells get more Cs at lower capex.

title: Corrugated cardboard flutes: sub-layer recess multiplies tier capacitor area
idea: Deposit each tier's capacitor slab as a fluted superlattice of thin alternating sublayers; after the single added mask opens the capacitor slot, a selective lateral recess etches alternate sublayers to corrugate the slot walls like cardboard flutes, and ALD electrode/high-k/electrode lines the corrugations.
why: Facts 1 and 2: 2-3x capacitor area per lateral 3D cell with no per-tier masks, reaching ~5 fF at shorter lateral length and tighter pitch.

title: Single grayscale exposure carves the entire 3D DRAM staircase
idea: Po: one exposure makes every layer. A multi-tone grayscale mask and a linear-contrast resist print a ramp of resist heights in one shot, and a proportional-selectivity etch transfers it into all 26-100 tier landing steps at once instead of dozens of trim-etch cycles.
why: 3D DRAM manufacturability (fact 2) and litho count: staircase from tens of trim-etch loops to ~1-3 litho+etch, ~5x cheaper, unlocking high tier counts.

title: Grayscale exposure etches every 3D tier contact in one step
idea: Ideal: a 3D array whose tier contacts cost one step. Closest: for a capacitorless 3D floating-body or gain-cell stack, replace the multi-mask trim-and-etch wordline staircase with one grayscale (variable-dose) exposure that makes a resist ramp of N heights; a proportional etch transfers it, opening every tier's landing at once.
why: Facts 2 and 4: staircases cost one litho/etch loop per 4-8 tiers plus array-edge area; a single ramp removes ~10-20 masks at 64+ tiers, and thin capacitorless tiers keep the ramp shallow.

title: Re-patternable EUV mask blanks: strip absorber, keep the multilayer
idea: First principle: an EUV mask's value is its defect-free Mo/Si multilayer blank, and the pattern is just information in the absorber. Add an etch-stop capping layer so the absorber can be stripped without damaging the blank, and rewrite the same blank with a new pattern when a design is revised.
why: Mask cost (fact 4): the blank is a large share of EUV reticle cost, so reuse cuts mask spend ~40%.

title: Plate-less holographic print plus one cookie-cutter trim mask
idea: Expose the hexagonal storage-node array by three-beam immersion interference (no mask, perfect periodicity, one spacer pitch split), then use exactly one cheap DUV cookie-cutter mask to blank the pattern outside mats and at mat edges.
why: Fact 4: removes the EUV array-hole layer; interference exposure tools cost roughly a tenth of EUV, with lower roughness and no reticle defects in the array.

title: Ephemeral-grade dies: retention-failing DRAM sold for TTL-bounded data
idea: TRIZ #27 Cheap short-living objects: dies that fail the 64 ms retention screen but hold data for 4-8 ms are sold as E-grade parts with refresh logic fused off, and the runtime places only data with a hard time-to-live below the rated window (collective-communication buffers, prefetch staging, pipeline handoffs), invalidating pages at expiry.
why: Zero refresh power; recovers the ~3-8% retention yield loss and skips the long hot retention-pause tests that dominate DRAM test time (~20-30% test-cost and tester-capex cut) (facts 3, 4).

title: PFAS-free fab plumbing using polyolefin, PEEK, metal seals and dry pumps
idea: Extreme user: implant-device makers demanding fully PFAS-free supply chains. Replace PFA/PTFE/PVDF wetted parts with high-purity HDPE/PP, PEEK, quartz and electropolished stainless, FFKM o-rings with metal/EPDM seals, and PFPE-oil pumps with dry screw pumps.
why: Policy-proofs the fab against EU/US PFAS bans that could otherwise stop a line; small cost, large continuity value.

title: Nano-Velcro stacking: reworkable HBM dies swapped after test
idea: Replace permanent hybrid bonds with interlocking Cu nanowire hook-and-loop arrays grown in alumina templates that cold-weld under modest pressure yet allow controlled debond; test the stack, pull and replace failing dies, then anneal to make joints permanent.
why: Fact 6: recovers much of the 20-30% HBM stack yield loss instead of scrapping 8-16 good dies for one bad one.

title: Fluidic self-assembly drops DRAM dielets into glass interposers
idea: Revive Alien Technology's 1990s fluidic self-assembly, where shaped micro-chips in a slurry settle into matching wells: dice DRAM into ~0.3 mm keyed trapezoidal dielets that self-orient into wells on a large glass interposer next to an accelerator, then wire them with one panel RDL layer. Thousands of dielets assemble in seconds without pick-and-place or TSV stacking.
why: Fact 6 and capital: replaces HBM's TSV stack (3x area per bit, 20-30% yield loss) with planar known-good dielets at ~10 um RDL pitch; an assembly bath costs <$1M versus $50M+ hybrid-bonding lines.

title: Nanoimprint's overlay killer neutralized by alignment-free stacked crossbars
idea: Canon's nanoimprint for NAND stalled on overlay error and defects. Perpendicular line arrays need no overlay because every crossing is a cell wherever lines land, so imprint 15 nm half-pitch lines from daughter templates replicated off one e-beam master, stack 16 decks of amorphous-carbon sp2/sp3 switching cells with shared lines, and absorb random offsets with a per-array line calibration map.
why: Meets 100x: no EUV, imprint tools ~1/5 scanner cost, 16 decks of 4F2 cells; est. ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades: carbon-cell endurance and write energy, template wear, defect mapping.

title: Remote epitaxy through graphene lets one template seed hundreds of tiers
idea: Worse: consume a fresh single-crystal substrate for every device layer. Flip: grow single-crystal oxide or III-N films through a graphene interlayer on a reusable sapphire/GaN template, peel each membrane off with a Ni stressor, and stack the membranes as 3D memory tiers. The template is reused for every peel.
why: 3D DRAM (fact 2): crystalline tiers without Si/SiGe epi stacks, with substrate cost amortized ~100x.

title: Asymmetric-pitch pillars let conformal gates self-merge into wordlines
idea: Box: MIM charge x vertical GAA pillar x voltage sense amp x 2D x Si x one dot mask with pitch_x below twice the gate thickness and pitch_y above it. Conformal ALD TiN merges between pillars along x into continuous wordlines but stays split along y, and an anisotropic spacer etch isolates rows, giving wordlines with no wordline mask and ~3 masks for the cell.
why: Mask count and overlay (fact 4) with a 4F2-like vertical cell from ALD and RIE; risk is wordline resistance of thin merged TiN and pillar CD variation.

title: SCALPEL electron projection prints DRAM arrays without EUV or neon
idea: Revive Bell Labs' 1990s SCALPEL, which projected a 4x-reduced image of a scattering-contrast membrane mask with 100 keV electrons: modern high-brightness cathodes, aberration-corrected optics and fast resists let it expose DRAM's repetitive array layers in vacuum. Its source is a hot cathode, so there is no excimer neon and no EUV drive-laser helium.
why: Fact 4 under the constraint: replaces 5-7 EUV layers with tools targeted at ~$30-50M versus $200M+ for EUV. Risks are space-charge blur and throughput (~20-40 wafers/hour).

title: 2050 engineer: confined-nucleation MoS2 grown at 300 C as access transistors
idea: A 2050 engineer grows channels instead of etching them. Low-temperature MOCVD (<=350 C) of monolayer MoS2 or WSe2 inside litho-defined pockets that confine nucleation to one grain per pocket forms the access transistors of each stacked memory tier, grown tier by tier within the BEOL thermal budget.
why: A ~1.8-2 eV gap and an atomically thin channel could push leakage below 1 fA (fact 3), relaxing refresh, while tiers grow sequentially with no bonding. High risk: contact resistance, and low-temperature film quality.

title: Self-stratifying paint: one-coat multilayer litho stacks
idea: Industrial coatings use self-stratifying paints that separate into primer and topcoat in one application; formulate a single spin-on film that, during bake, segregates by surface energy into a silicon-rich hardmask bottom layer, an organic underlayer and a fluorinated-segment resist top layer.
why: Process steps and track capex (fact 4): saves ~2 coats and bakes per patterned layer across ~40 litho layers, ~5-8% fewer total steps and less chemical use.

title: Deposition sets density: 128-tier DRAM strings from 180 nm holes
idea: Inverts 'density comes from lithography'. Deposit 128 alternating oxide/poly (or Si/SiGe) tiers, punch 180 nm channel holes with a KrF stepper and 1990s deep-trench RIE (AR ~36:1), and form one ring-gate transistor plus lateral-recess capacitor per tier per hole, with staircase contacts made by repeated resist-trim etching.
why: Each 0.13 um2 hole holds 128 cells, ~1,000 nm2 per bit versus ~860 nm2 for a 6F2 cell at 12 nm, with no EUV; capital moves to cheap deposition tools (facts 2, 4).

title: Superionic silver-sulfide stamps electrochemically etch metal lines without resist
idea: Effect: solid-state ion migration in a superionic conductor. A Ag2S stamp patterned once is pressed onto a Ag or Cu film under bias, and Ag+ ions move into the stamp only at contact points, removing metal with ~10 nm fidelity with no resist and no plasma etch. $1M demonstrates bitline-pitch metal patterning on 100 mm wafers.
why: Fact 4 and capital: one stamp station replaces coat, expose, develop, etch and strip for metal layers; Cu or Ag lines also avoid tungsten (~80% from China).

title: Inline print-test-repair loop with capacitive probe rollers
idea: Magnify test throughput by running the web past non-contact capacitive probe rollers that map bad blocks in real time; a downstream laser cuts and a printer reroutes around them before lamination.
why: Yield and test capital: testing at web speed removes probe-card floors and turns defects into reroutes, not scrap.

title: Frugal homesteader: implant-free junctionless fab with no furnaces
idea: A homesteader without tractors designs around the missing tool. Make every transistor in the memory tiers junctionless or Schottky-contacted (as-deposited doped oxide or poly channels thinned for off-state, metal-silicide contacts), so no dopant-activation anneal is ever needed and the fab owns no ion implanters, diffusion furnaces or RTP.
why: Implanters and furnaces are ~10-15% of front-end capex and many steps; a <=400 C, implant-free tool list (~25 vs ~45 tool types) cuts capital and opens the market to non-semiconductor tool vendors. Risk: junctionless off-current tail vs refresh (fact 3).

title: Eliminate the tall capacitor: short storage nodes plus offset-cancelling sense amps
idea: Halve capacitor height (AR ~35:1, Cs ~2.5 fF) and recover margin with offset-cancelled, bitline-isolated sense amplifiers and shorter bitlines, absorbing the extra refresh inside the existing DDR5 refresh budget. The die still runs standard DDR5 timings.
why: Fact 1: halves the hardest etch, removes support-lattice steps and pillar-collapse loss; capacitor-module cost down ~30-40%, partly paid back in sense-amp area.

title: Hyperscalers consign their own tools inside memory fabs
idea: Inverts 'the fab owns its capital'. A cloud buyer purchases a block of scanners and etchers, consigns them into a memory maker's line, and receives that block's output at cash cost plus a tolling fee, as in chemical tolling.
why: Moves ~$2-5B of capex per block off the memory maker's balance sheet, lowering its cost of capital and letting capacity start with demand rather than after it.

title: Hot wafer-sort at 150 C replaces package burn-in ovens
idea: Under 125 C for 10 years: test retention on 150 C hot chucks at wafer sort to map each die's leakage tail, fuse weak rows into redundancy and burn a per-bank temperature-refresh table into eFuses, so no packaged burn-in is needed and every shipped die is pre-screened 25 C beyond its rating.
why: Back-end capital: removes burn-in boards, ovens and ~48 h cycles (~3-5% of cost) while guaranteeing the 125 C retention tail.

title: Brain-fold gyrification: build cells on deep corrugated wafer sidewalls
idea: The cortex triples its area by folding; etch the wafer once into 1.2 um tall fins at 120 nm pitch (ArF plus spacer doubling), then build cells on both sidewalls using only conformal ALD and horizontal bands defined by repeated deposit-fill-recess cycles, so every band along the fin height is a row of cells.
why: Sidewall area is ~20x the footprint; even at half the planar cell efficiency that is ~10x bits/mm2, with the extra area coming from cheap deposition/recess cycles rather than EUV (fact 4).

title: Orrery: orbital-current torque in light metals replaces heavy-metal SOT lines
idea: Random stimulus 'orrery' (orbits drive the motion) -> SOT-MRAM write lines use the orbital Hall effect in abundant light metals (Ti, Cr or oxidized Cu), with a Ni-based conversion layer that turns orbital current into torque on the free layer. This replaces beta-tungsten, Pt or Ta spin-Hall lines.
why: Non-volatile SOT-MRAM keeps unlimited endurance (no barrier current) and sub-ns writes. It removes tungsten and PGM dependence, and lower-resistivity lines cut write energy and driver area.

title: Embossed relief: one grayscale mask prints three cell levels
idea: Like a relief-embossing die that presses several heights at once, use one grayscale multi-transmission mask on a multi-threshold resist to print landing-pad, bitline-contact and storage-node patterns as three resist heights, then transfer them by sequential etch-back so each level opens self-aligned to the others.
why: Fact 4: adds one mask yet retires two to three critical exposures and their overlay budget; ~5-8% wafer cost reduction.

title: Vertical CCD strings in a 3D-NAND stack, four phase contacts
idea: Revive 1970s CCD serial memory (Fairchild F464, Intel 2416), which needed no contact or access transistor per bit, as vertical charge-coupled strings: a 3D-NAND-style alternating oxide/gate stack is etched once for channel holes, and every fourth gate layer is tied to the same clock phase so charge packets march up the hole to a sense node at the top. With only four phase lines, the staircase and per-tier contacts disappear.
why: Fact 2 and capital: one critical hole mask for ~200 tiers, no staircase (10+ masks and trims in 3D NAND) and no capacitor pillar; shifting at ~2 GHz gives ~50 ns average latency, and recirculation doubles as refresh. Risk is charge-transfer efficiency and dark current in a deposited channel liner.

title: Regenerable release coating extends imprint template life tenfold
idea: First principle: template wear happens in the top few nm where contact occurs, so the template body never needs replacing if its surface can be renewed. Coat imprint templates with a ~2 nm ALD sacrificial layer (Al2O3 plus fluorinated SAM) that is stripped and redeposited every ~1,000 imprints to restore the exact CD.
why: Mask/template cost for EUV-free imprint (fact 4): ~10x lower template cost per wafer.

title: Thickness-defined vertical IGZO 3D DRAM on Gen-8.5 display glass
idea: Box: oxide gain-cell node charge x vertical IGZO TFT whose channel length is a deposited film thickness x current sensing x 48-tier monolithic stack x Gen-8.5 glass panel x i-line display lithography plus ALD. Every critical dimension (gate length, dielectric, node) comes from film thickness or recess time rather than resolution, so 1.5 um display steppers suffice and bits/area come from tier count on a 5.5 m2 substrate (~75x a 300 mm wafer).
why: Capital intensity and U.S. manufacturability: borrows the display-fab cost model ($/m2 processed ~10-30x below DRAM fabs); claims 5-10x lower capex per bit for a capacity tier; risk is panel-scale ALD uniformity and per-tier density.

title: Etch-free, lift-off-only 2T0C gain cell from evaporated ultrathin oxides
idea: Box: gate-node charge x ultrathin (3-4 nm) evaporated In2O3 write FET plus p-type SnO read FET x current sensing x 2D/BEOL x any substrate x additive lift-off only, no plasma etching. Every layer is evaporated or sputtered through patterned resist and lifted off, with an oxygen-plasma-free ozone anneal setting carrier density, so the flow needs an aligner, evaporator and sputterer only.
why: Process capital: removes etch tools and their gases from the flow while giving a complementary gain cell whose ultrathin channel keeps off-current low; risk is lift-off resolution and SnO stability.

title: Park the dielectric at its antiferroelectric transition for k above 100
idea: Ideal: a dielectric with infinite k so the capacitor needs no height. Closest: an antiferroelectric ZrO2-rich HfZrO film whose field-induced AFE-to-FE transition is centered at the plate bias, so the small storage-voltage swing rides the steep part of the P-E curve for k_eff ~100-150.
why: Fact 1: k ~70 is the stated requirement; at k_eff ~100 pillar AR drops from ~70:1 to ~30:1, deleting the hardest etch/deposition loops and the anti-collapse support layers.

title: Short-loop CCD memory: charge shifts instead of transistors
idea: Inverts 'each bit needs its own access transistor and contact'. Store bits as charge packets in 64-stage recirculating CCD loops with spacer-defined overlapping poly gates; a loop is randomly addressed and streamed out in ~64 x 1 ns, and recirculation doubles as refresh.
why: No cell contacts, capacitor module or leakage-tail access transistors (facts 1, 3); ~2F2 per bit at spacer-defined gate pitch from 180 nm litho; latency is loop-length-bound.

title: Rotate the stack: film thickness becomes linewidth
idea: Rearrange the axes: deposit a 100-layer superlattice of alternating conductor/dielectric films with atomic-scale thickness control, then slice it and bond it on its side so each film edge becomes a 5-15 nm line on the new surface.
why: Sub-10 nm periodic lines without any lithography; line pitch is set by ALD/epitaxy thickness with angstrom precision.

title: Self-assembly's defect killer made irrelevant by cell-level defect maps
idea: Directed self-assembly never met logic defect specs (<0.01/cm2). Accept raw lamellar block-copolymer line arrays with ~1% bad crossings; after fab a controller sweep writes a compressed per-array defect bitmap, and the memory controller skips bad sites through Bloom-filter lookups so the media never needs to be perfect.
why: Meets 100x: sub-10 nm lines from a coat/bake track with no EUV or imprint, stacked 16+ decks; est. <$0.1/GB. Trades: ~3% spare capacity, lookup latency, mapping time at test.

title: Substitute high-temperature epitaxy with laser-crystallized silicon above logic
idea: Deposit amorphous silicon over finished logic BEOL and melt-crystallize it with nanosecond excimer or green laser pulses that heat only the top ~100 nm (BEOL stays below 400 C), seeding grains through small vias; then build silicon access transistors and capacitors in this layer directly over compute.
why: Constraint: memory ~1 um above logic gives ~0.1 pJ/bit access (>20x below HBM) with silicon-like leakage; capital: excimer annealers are commodity tools from LTPS display lines.

title: Phototropic resistless patterning: exposed surface sites switch on growth
idea: Shoots grow toward light; coat the wafer with a monolayer of photolabile-capped amines (nitroveratryl-type groups) that 193/248 nm light uncaps, and only uncapped sites nucleate ALD of the hardmask or metal. The pattern is grown directly, with no resist coat, bake, develop, strip or descum.
why: Removes ~6-8 steps and the track tool per patterned layer; est. 30-40% shorter litho-module cycle time and chemical use (fact 4).

title: Print the array once; later layers grow onto it
idea: Inverts 'each layer is lithographically re-registered'. One EUV exposure defines the honeycomb of active pillars; wordline recess, storage-node contact, landing pad and capacitor are then built on it by area-selective ALD, selective epitaxy and spacer self-alignment, so the pattern is inherited rather than re-printed.
why: Removes 3-5 of the 5-7 EUV layers and their overlay budgets (fact 4); ~20-30% lower litho capex per wafer.

title: Sn: tin-oxo resist doubles as hardmask, leaves as stannane
idea: Vapor-deposit a Sn-oxo-carbon resist, dry-develop it, keep the remaining SnOx as the etch hardmask, then remove it with an H2 plasma that converts tin into volatile SnH4 (the trick used to clean EUV collectors).
why: Water: no spin solvent, TMAH develop, rinse or wet strip on each patterned layer (>10x litho-module water cut) and one fewer hardmask deposition per layer.

title: Nespresso pods: sealed precursor cartridges for micro-fab ALD
idea: Borrowed from coffee pods that made espresso possible without a barista: package each ALD precursor (TEMAZ, TMA, TiCl4) in sealed, barcoded, heated single-use cartridges with built-in vapor regulation that click into a tool manifold, so a small fab skips bulk chemical delivery, gas cabinets and abatement plumbing.
why: Capital: bulk specialty-chemical systems are ~10% of fab capex and months of build; cartridges let small U.S. pilot fabs start in weeks.

title: Molecular self-assembly prints the capacitor lattice instead of EUV
idea: Scale shift from scanner optics down to molecular length: a high-chi block copolymer (PS-b-PDMS or PS-b-PMMA) self-assembles into a hexagonal cylinder lattice that matches the honeycomb capacitor array, registered by an ArF-immersion guide pattern at 4x pitch; sequential infiltration synthesis turns one block into an alumina hardmask for the hole etch.
why: Removes 1-2 EUV exposures (capacitor hole, landing pad) from Fact 4; ~15-25% lower array litho cost per wafer because the molecule, not the scanner, sets the pitch.

title: Magnify the substrate: DRAM on Gen-8.5 display glass panels
idea: Magnify the substrate from a 300 mm wafer (0.07 m2) to a 2.2x2.5 m display-glass mother panel (~80x the area) and build oxide-TFT 2T gain-cell arrays on idle LCD/LTPO backplane lines, dicing panels into memory tiles bonded to silicon periphery.
why: Capital intensity and throughput: depreciated LCD fabs cost cents per cm2 versus ~$10+/cm2 for DRAM wafers; area cost per bit could fall 10x even at relaxed F, turning global display overcapacity into memory capacity.

title: Sort-time error syndromes replace most inline metrology
idea: Combine code-layer syndrome counters with advanced process control: every probed die reports spatial maps of corrected bits, which are decoded into virtual metrology (CD, overlay, etch depth inferred from error signatures). Inline CD-SEM/OCD sampling can then drop ~70%.
why: Metrology and inspection are ~10-12% of fab capex. The 1% budget makes the slower feedback loop acceptable (capital intensity, throughput).

title: Glassblowing silicon: hydrogen reflow seals stacked buried cavities for tiers
idea: Use surface-tension shaping like a glassblower: etch deep hole arrays with depth-modulated scallops, then hydrogen-anneal near 1100 C so silicon migrates and pinches each scallop into a sealed planar void (multi-level silicon-on-nothing), leaving stacked single-crystal Si plates that later receive gate and capacitor dielectrics.
why: Fact 2: single-crystal multi-tier silicon without the Si/SiGe superlattice epi that warps and dislocates beyond ~30-60 periods; one etch plus one anneal replaces ~100 epi layers.

title: Pearl: one seeded ferroelectric grain per cell kills variability
idea: Random stimulus 'pearl' (one crystal grows around one seed) -> a self-aligned nucleation seed (a ZrO2 or TiN facet) is planted at the bottom of each ferroelectric capacitor, so the HZO crystallizes as a single orthorhombic grain per cell instead of random multigrain.
why: Non-volatile FeRAM is currently sized for grain-induced variation of Pr and Ec. Single-grain cells could shrink 2-3x at the same litho (relaxed DUV instead of EUV) and cut wake-up and fatigue spread.

title: Eliminate the binary bit: ternary-charge cells give 58% more bits per mask
idea: Store three charge levels per cell (0, half and full VBLH) and read them with a two-reference successive-approximation sense amplifier; pairs of cells hold 9 states and encode 3 bits.
why: Litho and capital: ~50% more bits from the same mask stack and wafer, a 'free node' without EUV, paid for with sense margin and a higher refresh rate.

title: Two-angle stencil spraying: one mask, two self-aligned features
idea: Like a painter spraying one stencil from two angles to get two offset strokes, pattern one resist-bridge mask and perform double-angle directional deposition (Dolan-bridge style) so each opening yields two offset, self-aligned features, e.g. access gate plus storage contact, or two cells per opening.
why: Fact 4: halves critical masks for paired features and removes their overlay; ~2x pattern density from one DUV mask.

title: Sea-urchin amorphous precursor infiltration crystallizes high-k inside pores
idea: Sea urchins fill spine molds with a liquid-like amorphous carbonate and crystallize it in place; flow a polymer-stabilized liquid amorphous titanate precursor into capacitor holes by capillarity, then crystallize it to rutile TiO2 or SrTiO3 (k 80-150) at low temperature on a thin seed liner that templates the phase.
why: Delivers k~100 (fact 1) with a spin-and-bake instead of slow ALD supercycles; est. 5x faster dielectric module and a shorter, easier-to-etch capacitor.

title: Aerospace anodizing: aluminum-oxide nanopore templates for capacitors
idea: Instead of EUV plus deep plasma etch of 60-75:1 holes, deposit thick aluminum, nanoimprint shallow seed pits, and anodize it in oxalic or sulfuric acid (aircraft anodizing chemistry) so ordered vertical pores grow 1-3 um deep, then line them with TiN/ZrO2-Al2O3/TiN. Elements: Al, O, S, C, Ti, Zr, N only.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1) and etch capex (fact 4): AR ~115 is trivial for anodization; a ~$1M wet bath replaces $5-10M high-AR etchers; no W or Ru.

title: Honeycomb anodic alumina self-orders capacitor holes at extreme aspect
idea: Bees build hexagonal comb from local wall rules; sputter aluminum over the landing pads and anodize it, so pores self-organize into a hexagonal lattice whose pitch is set by voltage (25-60 nm) and whose sites are pinned by shallow DUV-printed dimples on the pads; pores grow 5-10 um deep in a wet bench, then get ALD electrode and dielectric.
why: Replaces the capacitor-hole exposure and hardest plasma etch (facts 1, 4) with a ~$100k anodization bench; aspect ratio becomes nearly free, removing the charge wall.

title: Holographic grating writer: mask-free interference lithography for array lattices
idea: Borrowed from holographic diffraction-grating production, which uses interfering laser beams instead of masks. Because DRAM array layers (active, buried wordline, capacitor lattice) are strictly periodic, expose them with 3-6-beam 193 nm immersion interference at ~70 nm pitch, spacer-double to ~35 nm, and use one coarse trim exposure to cut array edges.
why: Fact 4: array critical layers become maskless and EUV-free; interference optics are simple (~1/10 scanner cost) with very high throughput.

title: Periphery micro-tiles fall into place by fluidic self-assembly
idea: Po: the transistors find their own seats. Make sense-amp/decoder micro-tiles on a cheap logic process, dice them into shape-keyed blocks, and flow them over array wafers with matching etched recesses where shape and capillary forces seat them; one RDL then wires them in.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): array wafers carry only cells, roughly doubling bits per DRAM-fab wafer while periphery comes from cheaper nodes.

title: Solar project finance: offtake-backed DRAM fab special-purpose vehicles
idea: Finance each fab like a utility-scale solar farm: a special-purpose vehicle owns the fab, hyperscalers sign 10-year take-or-pay bit offtake contracts at indexed prices (like PPAs), and the transferable advanced-manufacturing investment credit is sold to tax-equity buyers, so the fab borrows non-recourse debt at infrastructure rates.
why: Cost of capital: WACC from ~10-12% to ~6-7% cuts the capital charge in wafer cost by ~25-30%; offtake removes the boom-bust risk that stops fabs from being built.

title: Hyperscaler-financed tool SPVs backed by wafer-start futures
idea: Worse: make memory makers carry all depreciation risk so they underinvest at the start of every boom. Flip: hyperscalers buy tradable forward contracts for wafer starts on named tool sets. The contracts collateralize tool-level project finance: each scanner or etcher is owned by an SPV and leased to the fab, off its balance sheet.
why: Capital intensity: depreciation is ~55% of wafer cost; cutting the cost of capital from ~12% to ~6% lowers wafer cost ~10-15% and speeds capacity adds.

title: Z-NAND's failure fixed: erase-free 64-byte sub-page flash over CXL
idea: Samsung Z-NAND and Kioxia XL-Flash failed to win DRAM sockets because 4 KB pages and block erases left them neither cheap nor fast enough. Build an SLC die with 512-byte mini-page sense amps per plane, append 64 B cachelines as log writes into pre-erased blocks, erase in idle planes, and absorb rewrites in a 1% DRAM front, exposed as CXL.mem.
why: Meets ~50-100x: ~$0.1-0.15/GB SLC-class cost serving warm DRAM data. Trades: 1-3 us misses, ~1e5 SLC endurance hidden by the DRAM front and wear-leveling.

title: Mass-produced fab modules: build factories like ships, not cathedrals
idea: Worse: build each fab as a bespoke 5-year megaproject. Flip: design a 5k-wafer/month DRAM fab module where tools sit in sealed N2 minienvironments linked by enclosed transport, so no ballroom cleanroom is needed. Build identical modules on an assembly line and drop them onto prepared pads.
why: Capital/time: the cleanroom shell (~25-30% of fab capex) goes away, time to first wafer falls from ~4 to ~1.5 years, and replication drives the module learning curve.

title: Crystal planes do the etching: KOH slot capacitors
idea: Inverts 'high-aspect-ratio etch needs plasma tools'. In (110) silicon, KOH/TMAH wet etching stops on vertical {111} planes, giving atomically smooth slots >100:1 deep from stepper-defined (spacer-narrowed) openings; lined with dielectric they form deep slot capacitors that share walls between neighbouring cells.
why: Hits AR ~115 (fact 1) on a ~$200k wet bench instead of $5M+ etchers; density still needs sub-litho line pitch from a companion trick.

title: Cavendish Kinetics' stiction problem inverted into a refresh-free NEMS bit
idea: Cavendish Kinetics' MEMS memory fought stiction and pivoted away. Make stiction the storage: back-end nano-cantilevers latch by van der Waals force onto a contact (1) or rest open (0) and are released by a pull-off electrode, and the electromechanical hysteresis window rejects half-selected cells so a passive crossbar needs no transistor.
why: Refresh-free with zero standby leakage (fact 3); metal-and-dielectric-only BEOL process at ~3 masks per deck, stackable over periphery, no front-end area.

title: X-ray lithography's mask killer dodged with interference-only array exposure
idea: Proximity X-ray lithography died mainly because 1x masks could not be made or inspected. DRAM arrays are periodic, so print line/space and hexagonal hole lattices by mask-free interference of 2-4 coherent EUV/soft X-ray beams split from one compact free-electron-laser source feeding 10+ exposure stations, trimmed by cheap DUV cut masks.
why: Removes EUV scanners from ~4 of the 5-7 EUV layers; one source amortized over many stations and huge depth of focus cut cost per array layer several-fold.
